value: This article explores semigroups and monoids, algebraic structures intermediate between magmas and groups. A semigroup is defined as a set with an associative binary operation, while a monoid further includes an identity element. The text details their fundamental properties, including their potentially non-commutative nature, substructures like ideals, and various types of homomorphisms and congruences. It also covers important structural aspects, such as idempotents, maximal subgroups, and numerous special classes of semigroups. Historically, the formal study of semigroups began in the early 20th century, and the article highlights their significant applications across theoretical computer science (e.g., finite automata), probability theory (Markov processes), and the study of partial differential equations.
